name: Central bank stress
value: BoE at 4%; Fed eyes 50bp; yen near 160
summary: Central banks tighten against energy-driven inflation as the White House presses the Fed; Japan warns on the yen
state: Markets weigh a rare 50bp Fed rise at the 8–9 Dec meeting after a third above-forecast CPI print, while President Trump wants cuts and Treasury Secretary Bessent has argued against much tightening (The Edge Malaysia, 17 Nov). Japan's officials warned on 12–13 Nov as the yen neared 160 per dollar; no November intervention has been reported, the last being from 30 Jul to 26 Aug (FXStreet). The Bank of England raised Bank Rate to 4% on 5 Nov (Bank of England). No emergency move or attempt to remove a central-bank head was found as of 25 Nov.
for_you: Borrowers in the US, UK and euro area face rising rather than falling interest rates. Currency moves around the yen may stay volatile while Japan warns of action.
rubric_hit: Watch: stagflationary dilemma and open political pressure on the Fed; no emergency moves for Alert

sources.title: The Edge Malaysia — Fed under Warsh weighs hike as inflation stays sticky

why: Central banks are the shock absorbers; when they are boxed in or their independence is challenged, markets lose their backstop.
drivers: Inflation vs growth trade-off, political pressure, currency moves, financial stability.

rubric.alert: Emergency inter-meeting moves, attempt to remove a central-bank head, or coordinated intervention.
rubric.watch: Stagflationary dilemma, open political pressure on a major central bank, or FX intervention by a G7 bank.
rubric.normal: Fed, ECB and BoJ acting orderly and on schedule; independence unquestioned.
